smithery.note: first_seen is the date THIS drift-tracking clock started (when check-external-listings.sh's classification scheme was built), not the date Smithery's listing was originally published (listing_published, Mar 12 — correct then, ~95 tools). Using the publish date as first_seen would make this ALREADY 30+ days old and wrongly block on day one. Description field is set once at first publish, Settings-UI-only edit, no CLI/API override. See docs/OPERATOR-ACTION-smithery-listing-description.md. Fable ruling 2026-09-02 (T-30 dispute q-1, Q2.3): once the description text carries no tool-count number, check-external-listings.sh treats it as no-drift permanently — this entry then stops mattering.

official_registry.note: ZZ-03-10 (D-2/R1+R2, docs/03-SPECIFICATION.md §D-2). first_seen is 03-SPECIFICATION.md's analysis date (2026-09-14), matching Fable's own stated escalation deadline of 2026-10-14 for this whole track (+30 days) — not the date this JSON entry was committed. server.json's description was fixed (numbers removed) in this same commit; the live registry record still shows the old '327 tools, 92 providers' string until the operator runs `mcp-publisher publish` as step 2 of R4's gated npm -> Official Registry -> Glama -> Smithery republish order. check-external-listings.sh reports this as status pending_republish, not drift, while it waits — see the script's own ZZ-03-10 header comment. Escalates (blocking=true) only if R4 still hasn't run by 2026-10-14.

glama_health.note: ZZ-03-10 (D-2/R2, R3 tracked separately). Glama's connector page (glama.ai/mcp/connectors/io.github.whiteknightonhorse/apibase) shows a binary Status field independent of its description text (which is Official-Registry-synced and covered by the official_registry entry above) — confirmed Unhealthy as of 2026-09-14 (02-RESEARCH.md §2.10/§2.12, reproduced via curl raw HTML + WebFetch). pulsemcp.note: ZZ-03-10 (D-2/R6). PulseMCP's listing shows materially wrong content ('API development platform with testing, monitoring, and documentation tools' — not a stale number, a wrong description entirely) and the site was, as of 02-RESEARCH.md §2.9/§2.12, refusing new submissions while redesigning listing management. Both the public page and the documented v0.1 API (which additionally needs a key this repo doesn't hold) are Cloudflare-blocked against automated fetches from this repo's CI/server context — check-external-listings.sh reports pulsemcp as unreachable, which is the expected steady state, not a signal to retry. R6 is the operator manually checking PulseMCP's status 7 days after R4 completes, then (if still wrong) sending a fleet-drafted correction request. This entry's 30-day clock is a backstop, not the R6 timeline itself.
